description: Edit an automation (name, sender or `category`, trigger incl. trigger.cooldown_seconds, or steps). `steps` replaces every step; `step` replaces just the one with its id. Pass `if_updated_at` (the updated_at you read): an edit made by someone else since then answers 409 instead of being overwritten.

category.description: What it sends: marketing, alerts (transactional) or codes (otp). With no `from`, TextKit picks a number approved for this. Falls back to a built-in topic.

from.description: One of your numbers, to pin the flow to it. Leave it out and TextKit picks a number approved for `category`. A sandbox number makes it a sandbox flow.

if_updated_at.description: The automation's `updated_at` as you read it. If it changed since (another edit), nothing is saved and the answer is 409: read it again and redo the edit on the latest.

step.description: One of: send_sms {body, from?, send_time?, max_wait_seconds?}; wait {seconds}; wait_for_event {event, timeout_seconds, on_received, on_timeout}; condition {check, on_met, on_not_met}; end. Branches are "continue", "end", or "goto:<id of a later step>".

body.description: send_sms. Merge fields: event properties by name, {{first_name}}, {{name}}, {{phone}}, {{field:<custom>}}.

check.description: {kind: event_received, event} | {kind: property, property, op, value?} | {kind: contact_field, field, op, value?}. op: eq, neq, contains, gt, lt, exists, not_exists.

event.description: wait_for_event: the event to wait for

id.description: Stable handle for goto branches; assigned when omitted.

max_wait_seconds.description: send_sms with optimal_user_time, required: the longest this text may wait for that hour

on_met.description: condition: where to go when the check passes: continue, end, or goto:<step id>

on_not_met.description: condition: where to go when the check fails: continue, end, or goto:<step id>

on_received.description: wait_for_event: where to go when the event arrives: continue, end, or goto:<step id>

on_timeout.description: wait_for_event: where to go when time runs out: continue, end, or goto:<step id>

seconds.description: wait: how long, from 60 seconds to 30 days

send_time.description: send_sms: `optimal_user_time` waits for the hour this person usually replies or clicks, inside quiet hours. Default: right_away. Refused for one-time codes and order or shipping texts.

timeout_seconds.description: wait_for_event: how long to wait, from 60 seconds to 30 days

items.description: One of: send_sms {body, from?, send_time?, max_wait_seconds?}; wait {seconds}; wait_for_event {event, timeout_seconds, on_received, on_timeout}; condition {check, on_met, on_not_met}; end. Branches are "continue", "end", or "goto:<id of a later step>".

topic_id.description: Skip recipients unsubscribed from this topic.

trigger.description: What starts a run: an event, with optional filters

cooldown_seconds.description: Optional. After a run starts for a person, they do not start another for this long (for events that repeat, like a paywall view).

event.description: The tracked event that starts a run

filters.description: Up to 5 checks on the event's properties. All must hold

op.description: eq, neq, contains, gt, lt, exists or not_exists

value.description: The value to compare with. Not used by exists or not_exists

name: update_automation
title: Update automation
